sasha: FYI - spotted funcall oscillation on fenris-liteq int8 canary after the kernel swap. outputs are flipping between an empty repair array and a valid toolcall payload every other request. posting sample trace.

andre: ugh, can you drop the traces?

sasha: ```trace_id=abc123
request_id=xyz789
model=fenris-liteq:int8
step=1 response=TOOL_CALL {"action":"search","args":[]}
step=2 response=REPAIR []
step=3 response=TOOL_CALL {"action":"search","args":[{"q":"pizza"}]}
step=4 response=REPAIR []
```

tia: hmm looks like kv-prefix truncation at first glance, but the alternating pattern suggests a decoding path flip (repair heuristic kicking on some token sequences). could be the new aten kernel's padding behavior changing tokenization boundary checks.

jkramer: quick hypothesis: quant softmax rounding changed meaningfully -> token-level entropy flips and our funcall-detector threshold toggles. can we mirror the same requests on float16 kernel for 1k samples and diff funcall signatures?

sasha: starting mirror run now (small batch) and attaching logs when done. also pinging @ml-ci-bot to schedule a full spectral test.

ml-ci-bot: scheduled job fenris-oscillation-spectral-test #4412 -> started. estimated 25m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

tia: if hypothesis holds we should try two quick experiments: 1) set softmax_clip=1e-6 in canary; 2) run deterministic sampling for 500 requests and compare. low-cost first: toggle softmax_clip and re-run a short canary.

andre: +1. also capture per-token logits + funcall-prob on the problematic span so we can correlate rounding jumps.

sasha: will do. will update thread with mirror diffs and attached csvs when available.
